# Fixture — `slice-map`

Data for the renderer behind `/essentials:slice-map --html`, and the oracle that renders it. It is
**data, not a project**: no sources, no build.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `sample-data.json` | A hand-written, synthetic two-context instance of the data contract in `commands/slice-map.md` §6 |
| `sample-data-cycle.json`, `sample-data-twin.json`, `sample-data-scale.json` | Generated by `scripts/slice-index.py map` from `tests/slice-index/`; pinned by `tests/scripts/test_slice_index.py` |
| `expected.json` | Machine-readable expectations per data file, read by `render-check.py` |
| `render-check.py` | Renders each data file in headless Chrome (`--dump-dom`) and asserts on the DOM with the stdlib `html.parser` |
| `TEST-GUIDE.md` | The ground truth, including the rows only a person with a pointer can check |

The hand-written contexts (`orders`, `billing`) deliberately include things a healthy project would not
have — an aggregate written from two contexts, an event consumed by nobody's publisher, a cross-context
read with no `via:` — because a fixture holding only well-formed data cannot tell a correct renderer
from one that silently drops the awkward cases. They also carry one deliberately *healthy* shape: the
seven-node chain `PlaceOrder → orders.place_order → OrderPlaced → billing.payment_policy → IssueInvoice
→ billing.issue_invoice → InvoiceIssued`, which crosses a bounded context in the middle and fans out at
`OrderPlaced`.

## Running it

```bash
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py                  # all four data files + the unrendered trap
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py --keep /tmp/sm   # also keep the pages and DOM dumps
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py path/to/map.json # any slice-map JSON, generic checks only
```

Stdlib Python and one Chrome binary. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 harness error (unreadable
input, the placeholder line or the layout constants moved), **3 SKIPPED — no Chrome, nothing checked**.

Chrome is looked up as `--chrome`, `$CHROME_BIN`, then `chrome-headless-shell`, `google-chrome`,
`google-chrome-stable`, `chromium`, `chromium-browser`, `chrome` on `PATH`. Prefer
`chrome-headless-shell`, the Chrome for Testing build made for `--dump-dom`: all five pages check in
under a second with it. A full Chrome in headless mode is the fallback, and it is unproven: in a
container without a session bus it stalled on a trivial page, so CI should install
`chrome-headless-shell` rather than rely on a runner's `google-chrome`. A page that does not return
within 60 s is retried once, then failed as a hang (G10).

After a change to the template or the data contract, run this, then check the by-eye rows of
`TEST-GUIDE.md` in a browser. After a change to `scripts/slice-index.py`, regenerate the three
generated files with `uv run --script tests/scripts/test_slice_index.py --update-golden`, review the
diff, and run this again.
